version.changelog: 按第一二三批对照表更新上架名与渠道

llm.summary: The skill’s face-swap purpose is coherent, but it asks the agent to install and auto-upgrade an unpinned global npm tool that handles API tokens and media files.

dimensions.detail: The CLI is expected for the stated purpose, but it processes local media paths, uploads media, and uses a Qinghu API token after being installed from a mutable package source.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install path uses global npm installation, npx fallback, and automatic @latest upgrades for @iqinghu/qhkit without a pinned version or integrity record, so reviewed behavior can change at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Trigger wording includes broad terms like changing a person or replacing a character, but the body narrows usage to model/face replacement and separates clothing or pose changes into other skills.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, service, scheduler, or privilege escalation is present, but the artifact does normalize persistent user-level tool installation and mentions adding Node to shell startup configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact is clearly aimed at Qinghu AI e-commerce model and face replacement for images and videos, and it includes consent guidance for real-person likenesses.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing because the agent may install or upgrade @iqinghu/qhkit globally and then pass it your media files and Qinghu API token. Prefer a pinned, reviewed version in an isolated environment, avoid automatic @latest upgrades, and confirm you have rights to any real person’s likeness before using face replacement.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger terms are real, but they mostly align with the face/model replacement purpose and are partly bounded by capability notes later in the artifact.
[RP1] unexpected: Using the qhkit CLI is purpose-aligned, but unpinned npx execution is not necessary for the purpose and increases mutable dependency risk.
[RA2] expected: Installing Node in a user directory is a disclosed fallback and includes checksum verification, so this is downgraded from rogue-agent behavior to a persistence/proportionality note.
[T08] unexpected: The static finding is supported by the artifact: global unpinned npm install and @latest upgrade are present, with no lockfile, package pin, or integrity digest for the npm package.
